The primary 50% n=1000 result is scientifically informative despite the MEASUREMENT_INVALID status: TOST PASS with near-zero r=-0.003 and CI upper 0.059 strongly suggests the parent's 50% failure was a Type I error.

The NC-NULL-OVERLAP-0 failure (FP=0.025 vs threshold 0.01) is marginal: 12/480 noise samples scored above 0.20, but the noise distribution at 0% overlap (mu=0.095) should produce very few samples above 0.20. This may reflect sampling variance in the clamped Gaussian tail.

The RC-25%-TOST failure is the more concerning regression control issue: at 25% overlap with n=480, the correlation r=0.080 is exactly the same as the parent's 50% failure value, but now appearing at 25%. This suggests the orthogonality boundary may be around 25% overlap rather than 50%.

The non-monotonic orthogonality pattern (r strongest at 25%, not 50%) warrants investigation. A follow-up with n>=800 at 25% overlap could determine if this is sampling artifact or a real threshold effect.
